question.prompt: The sides of a regular polygon of \(n\) sides, \(n\gt4,\) are extended to form a star. The number of degrees at each point of the star is:

solutions.explanation:
Use the standard star construction: for each polygon side, extend its two neighboring sides until they meet outside the polygon. The original side and the two extensions form a triangle whose tip is a point of the star.

Let \(e\) be one exterior angle of the regular polygon. The exterior angles sum to \(360^\circ\), and regularity makes them equal, so
\[
e=\frac{360^\circ}{n}.
\]
Each base angle of the triangular point is supplementary to a polygon interior angle, so each equals \(e\). The triangle angle sum therefore gives the tip angle
\[
180^\circ-2e
=180^\circ-\frac{720^\circ}{n}
=\frac{180(n-4)}{n}^\circ.
\]
The condition \(n>4\) makes this angle positive. Thus the answer is \(\boxed{\dfrac{180(n-4)}{n}^\circ}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Exterior angles and a triangular point
